minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission presented its case for a fieldstone wall at North Cemetery; no vote was taken and a granite-post alternative was raised.
minutes.summary: The commission presented its plan to replace the pruned hundred-year-old hedge boundary at North Cemetery with a New England fieldstone wall, comparing it with hedge replacement on life-cycle cost. A resident, Dave Rogers, proposed looking at granite posts and chain like Sleepy Hollow in Concord and questioned using the stabilization fund. A select board member explained the ARPA reallocation plan. No formal votes were taken beyond opening and adjourning.

what_happened.line: The Cemetery Commission asked residents to back a fieldstone wall at North Cemetery by voting at the special town meeting on November 14, 2023.
The commission presented a plan to replace the pruned, century-old hedge boundary with a fieldstone wall and funding from ARPA money.
A life-cycle cost model shown to the meeting has the wall breaking even against hedges in about year 16.
A resident asked the commission to look at granite posts and chain; the commission said it is standing by the fieldstone wall.
A select board member said a special town meeting article would use the stabilization fund for vehicles, freeing ARPA money for other projects. No votes were taken.

why_it_matters: The wall would be paid from federal pandemic-relief (ARPA) money that other town projects also draw on, so spending it here leaves less for those, and residents will be asked to vote on it at town meeting.
watch_next: Special town meeting, November 14, 2023, at 7:00 pm: the vote on funding the North Cemetery wall and the stabilization fund article.
